4. Vertical mobility (Vertical Mobility)

By it is meant the change of the grade or post of a labourer, e.g. a constable, progressing and progressing, becomes a station-house officer, or a college lecturer progresses and becomes a principal.

Factors increasing mobility (Factors Affecting Mobility)

The causes increasing the mobility of labour are the following:

1. High wages

In the industries or sectors or areas in which wages are higher, workers will begin moving towards those industries and areas. For example in Pakistan people keep leaving villages and moving towards industrial areas, because in villages opportunities of employment are few and wages are low. Many Pakistanis, for the sake of higher wages, are doing jobs in America, Europe and Saudi Arabia.

2. Better terms of employment

The places and factories in which the terms (Terms) of work are better and suitable for labourers, labourers will move towards those very factories.

3. Education and skill

If labourers are educated and trained in technical terms, they can obtain jobs more or less at every place, office or factory. They face no difficulty in leaving one job and adopting another job. Therefore labourers being skilled too becomes a cause of increase in their mobility.

4. Means of transport

If means of coming and going are developed, labourers can easily come from one place to another place. In this way an increase occurs in the mobility of labour.

5. Desire for progress

If the spirit to progress exists in labourers, they keep searching for such works where they can get more remuneration than before, and they keep moving from one place to another place.

6. Peace and order

If there is peace and order in the country and there are no emergency conditions, labourers can come from one place to another place without fear and danger. In this way an increase occurs in the mobility of labour.

7. Awareness of conditions

If workers know what the opportunities of employment and jobs and the rates of wages are for them in different areas, they can go to suitable places in the light of this information. Government institutions can prove helpful in providing this information.

اگر آمد و رفت کے ذرائع ترقی یافتہ ہوں تو مزدور آسانی کے ساتھ، ایک مقام سے دوسرے مقام تک آ جا سکتے ہیں۔ یوں محنت کی نقل پذیری میں اضافہ ہوتا ہے۔

5۔ ترقی کی خواہش:

اگر مزدوروں کے اندر ترقی کرنے کا جذبہ موجود ہو تو وہ ایسے کاموں کی تلاش میں رہتے ہیں جہاں انہیں پہلے سے زیادہ معاوضہ مل سکے اور وہ ایک جگہ سے دوسری جگہ حرکت کرتے رہتے ہیں۔

اگر ملک میں امن و امان ہو، ہنگامی حالات نہ ہوں تو مزدور بلاخوف و خطر ایک جگہ سے دوسری جگہ آ جا سکتے ہیں۔ اس طرح محنت کی نقل پذیری میں اضافہ ہوتا ہے۔

اگر کارکنوں کو معلوم ہو کہ مختلف علاقوں میں ان کے لیے روزگار و ملازمت کے مواقع اور اُجرتوں کی شرحیں کیا ہیں، تو وہ ان معلومات کی روشنی میں مناسب مقام پر جا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ معلومات بہم پہنچانے میں سرکاری ادارے معاون ثابت ہو سکتے ہیں۔

4. Vertical mobility (Vertical Mobility)

By it is meant the change of the grade or post of a labourer, e.g. a constable, progressing and progressing, becomes a station-house officer, or a college lecturer progresses and becomes a principal.

Factors increasing mobility (Factors Affecting Mobility)

The causes increasing the mobility of labour are the following:

1. High wages

In the industries or sectors or areas in which wages are higher, workers will begin moving towards those industries and areas. For example in Pakistan people keep leaving villages and moving towards industrial areas, because in villages opportunities of employment are few and wages are low. Many Pakistanis, for the sake of higher wages, are doing jobs in America, Europe and Saudi Arabia.

2. Better terms of employment

The places and factories in which the terms (Terms) of work are better and suitable for labourers, labourers will move towards those very factories.

3. Education and skill

If labourers are educated and trained in technical terms, they can obtain jobs more or less at every place, office or factory. They face no difficulty in leaving one job and adopting another job. Therefore labourers being skilled too becomes a cause of increase in their mobility.

4. Means of transport

If means of coming and going are developed, labourers can easily come from one place to another place. In this way an increase occurs in the mobility of labour.

5. Desire for progress

If the spirit to progress exists in labourers, they keep searching for such works where they can get more remuneration than before, and they keep moving from one place to another place.

6. Peace and order

If there is peace and order in the country and there are no emergency conditions, labourers can come from one place to another place without fear and danger. In this way an increase occurs in the mobility of labour.

7. Awareness of conditions

If workers know what the opportunities of employment and jobs and the rates of wages are for them in different areas, they can go to suitable places in the light of this information. Government institutions can prove helpful in providing this information.

paras.text: Benefits of the mobility of labour (Advantages)

paras.text: 1. Reduction in unemployment
paras.urdu: 1۔ بے روزگاری میں کمی:
paras.pashto: 1. په بې‌روزګارۍ کې کمښت

paras.text: By virtue of the mobility of labour unemployment decreases, because if the demand for labourers becomes less in one industry, they can do jobs in other industries and can obtain employment by going to such places where workers are needed.

paras.text: Because of social mobility the division of caste is erased, mutual discord ends; educated people, without caring about their personal and family occupation, try to adopt a good job. In old times the concept of class division in terms of occupations, e.g. cobbler, oil-presser, barber, washerman, carpenter, blacksmith, weaver etc., has become faint, and now any of them, if he wishes, obtaining education or technical and mechanical training, can become an electrician, mechanic, plumber, accountant, lawyer, professor, doctor, engineer, civil servant etc. In its way there is no obstacle.

Benefits of the mobility of labour (Advantages)

1. Reduction in unemployment

By virtue of the mobility of labour unemployment decreases, because if the demand for labourers becomes less in one industry, they can do jobs in other industries and can obtain employment by going to such places where workers are needed.

2. End of prejudice

Because of social mobility the division of caste is erased, mutual discord ends; educated people, without caring about their personal and family occupation, try to adopt a good job. In old times the concept of class division in terms of occupations, e.g. cobbler, oil-presser, barber, washerman, carpenter, blacksmith, weaver etc., has become faint, and now any of them, if he wishes, obtaining education or technical and mechanical training, can become an electrician, mechanic, plumber, accountant, lawyer, professor, doctor, engineer, civil servant etc. In its way there is no obstacle.

3. Solution of over-population

By virtue of geographical mobility, the areas which are victims of over-population (Over-Population) (i.e. where people are in excess of employment opportunities), from there labourers move and go to such areas where there is a shortage of labourers.

4. Industrial progress

By virtue of mobility every industry can obtain labourers according to its need, and according to need experts too can be called from foreign countries.

Benefits of the mobility of labour (Advantages)

1. Reduction in unemployment

By virtue of the mobility of labour unemployment decreases, because if the demand for labourers becomes less in one industry, they can do jobs in other industries and can obtain employment by going to such places where workers are needed.

2. End of prejudice

Because of social mobility the division of caste is erased, mutual discord ends; educated people, without caring about their personal and family occupation, try to adopt a good job. In old times the concept of class division in terms of occupations, e.g. cobbler, oil-presser, barber, washerman, carpenter, blacksmith, weaver etc., has become faint, and now any of them, if he wishes, obtaining education or technical and mechanical training, can become an electrician, mechanic, plumber, accountant, lawyer, professor, doctor, engineer, civil servant etc. In its way there is no obstacle.

3. Solution of over-population

By virtue of geographical mobility, the areas which are victims of over-population (Over-Population) (i.e. where people are in excess of employment opportunities), from there labourers move and go to such areas where there is a shortage of labourers.

4. Industrial progress

By virtue of mobility every industry can obtain labourers according to its need, and according to need experts too can be called from foreign countries.

Problems of the rapid rate of population growth in Pakistan and the need of population education (Problems of HIGH rate of Population Growth and Need of Population Education)

Pakistan is the sixth largest country of the world in terms of population (6th most populous country in the world). In 1947, at the time of independence, the total population of (present western) Pakistan was three crore seventy lakh, which in this period of years has become 19 crore 17 lakh. As population increased, along with it the need of providing different goods and services, e.g. food, clothing, housing, education, hospitals, medicines and employment, too kept becoming more. The annual rate of population growth is 1.92%, although for developed countries it is 0.9 per cent and for developing countries 1.7 per cent.

1. Shortage of welfare facilities

Of the population of Pakistan 33 per cent of individuals work, but of them too 6.5 per cent are unemployed. In Pakistan the condition of housing facilities has become worse than before. At this time 70 lakh houses are fewer than needed: 25 lakh in urban areas and 45 lakh in rural areas. Its important reasons are these: the high rate of population growth and the migration of population from villages towards cities. At this time one room on average comes to the share of 3.5 individuals. In cities at this time there are 2,322 kachi abadis, in which one-fourth of the total urban population resides.
